title: Quarterly commitment plan and regression guardrails for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a compact, actionable quarterly commitment for Hosted API + Model Catalog that ties OKRs to verifiable signals (latency/cost/quality) and defines automated rollback/mitigation triggers.

Scope: 1) final model lineup and phasing for public catalog; 2) per-model rollout cadence and canary criteria; 3) regression guardrails (prompt-sets, perf SLOs, degradation trigger thresholds); 4) docs + runbook for support and sales. This ticket coordinates PM-level decisions, sign-offs, and the artifacts that eng/design will act on.

Key outcomes we are committing to by end of quarter: 1) a published model lineup with pinned versions and deprecation windows; 2) automated regression checks wired into CI that block releases reporting >5% BLEU drop or >10% latency tail increase for prioritized prompts; 3) a runbook for on-call and sales to follow when a model variant degrades; 4) a roadmap upload into the console release planner and partner-facing notice templates.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Conservative rollout (slow canaries) reduces regression risk but increases time-to-market for new models.
- Aggressive batching/quantization suggestions improve cost but may shift output distribution; we propose labeling quantized variants clearly in catalog and limiting auto-routing until we hit quality parity on eval sets.

Signals and gates (proposed):
- Canary pass: <=2% reduction in core prompt-set accuracy and <=5% 95th pct latency increase vs baseline.
- Full rollout gate: hourly eval pass for 48 hours + no critical customer regressions reported.
- Auto-fallback policy: route to last-green model variant when hourly fail rate >0.5% for production traffic or when on-call triggers escalation.

Artifacts and links:
- Draft commitment doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atl/confluence/hostedapi-q2-commitment (placeholder)
- Eval harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-evals/pull/2142
- Runbook stub (Drive): https://drive.redwood/drive/folders/hostedapi-runbooks-q2 (placeholder)
- Budget/cost model (sheet): https://sheets.redwood/reports/hosted-cost-q2 (placeholder)

Open questions for PM/Eng review:
1) Should we treat quantized variants as separate catalog entries or as attributes on the primary model? (eng prefers separate entries for routing simplicity).
2) Are the proposed SLO thresholds acceptable for enterprise customers with SLA needs? If not, define compensating controls (dedicated capacity or reserved lanes).
3) Do we set automated rollback to be immediate or require on-call approval for high-value customers?

Next steps (owner tags):
- PM (Aisha): finalize commitment doc and stakeholder review (due 2026-03-10) — COMPLETE
- Eng (Diego): wire hourly eval metric export to the dashboard and set up gating hooks in CI (ETA 2026-03-20) — IN PROGRESS
- Design (Maya Chen): create catalog labeling taxonomy and copy for variant pages (ETA 2026-03-18) — IN PROGRESS

Acceptance criteria for ticket closure: the commitment doc is approved by Eng, Design and GTM; CI gating is in place for the primary model candidates; runbook published and linked from catalog entries; rollout schedule uploaded to console release planner.
